To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HERMES effect is explained in a manner consistent with all relevant experimental constraints.

(a) a relativistic Lagrangian with $\omega,\sigma,\pi$ mesons, nucleons, and leptons can be used to describe the nucleon, meson, and lepton degrees of freedom in nuclei; (b) the Lagrangian can be used to compute the nuclear energy-momentum tensor, and the nucleon and meson components of the nuclear wave function can be obtained; (c) the nucleon-nucleus scattering cross section can be computed,

the HERMES effect is a manifestation of the coherent enhancement of the nuclear electroproduction cross section for longitudinal virtual photons, and that the enhancement is due to the presence of $\sigma,\omega,\pi$ meson components in the ground state nuclear wave function.
